_comment: Data/Learners/<learner_id>.json - one learner and their progress. Identity is a self-declared name or email with NO password: this identifies, it does not authenticate. Do not add anything to this file that would matter if the wrong person claimed the name.

learner_id._comment: Slug derived from the entered name or email, lowercased. Stable across sessions.

email._comment: Where a password-reset code is sent. null on accounts created before this existed - those cannot use Forgot password until an admin sets one from the People screen. Never used as the login name: the name is still the username.

password_reset._comment: An in-flight reset challenge. The CODE ITSELF IS NOT STORED - only a salted scrypt digest of it, the same treatment as the password, so a leaked record cannot be used to reset anyone. null when no reset is pending. Cleared on use, on expiry, and on too many wrong attempts.

attempts._comment: Wrong guesses so far. At 5 the challenge is discarded and a new code must be requested - a 6-digit code is only 1,000,000 wide, so unlimited guesses would be brute-forceable in minutes.

role._comment: Each role is a superset of the one before it. learner = the course. trainer = the course + the cohort dashboard. admin = both + the People screen, where roles are assigned. An id listed in studio.config.json `admins` is treated as admin whatever is stored here - the lockout escape hatch.

password._comment: Salted scrypt digest. NEVER leaves the server. null means the account is UNCLAIMED - a migrated record from before logins existed; the first person to sign in with that name sets the password and takes it.

certificate._comment: Written the first time every day of the course is complete, so the date on the certificate is stable and does not move if the learner reopens a day later. null until earned.

resume._comment: Where the landing page sends a returning learner. null for a learner who has enrolled but opened nothing.

progress._comment: Keyed 'w<week>d<day>'. A part completes when viewed; a day completes when all 4 of its parts have. attempted_problems records practice problems the learner has run code against.
